group_assessment.weighting: An ophthalmology research group working an experimental autoimmune glaucoma model in rats; WWOX is one of 24 microarray probes plus one follow-up qPCR, not a subject of the group. Credible for the model, not a WWOX group. Not a per-author sweep: weighting rests on the paper's own design.

entries.proposition: The microarray compared laser-microdissected inner retinal layers from three eyes per group.
entries.snippet: The laser microdissection was performed as described before by Plum et al., 2016, with minor changes (n = 3 eyes/group) [32].

entries.proposition: Table 4 lists the Wwox probe A_64_P028011 as down-regulated in immunised animals with p = 0.030 and a tabulated fold change of 0.864.
entries.snippet: A_64_P028011 Wwox Rattus norvegicus WW domain-containing oxidoreductase (Wwox), mRNA [NM_001106188] 0.030 0.864 (↓)

entries.proposition: Whole-retina RT-qPCR gave Wwox at 0.24-fold in immunised animals, p = 0.002.
entries.snippet: It was also found that the mRNA expression levels of Wwox were downregulated in the ONA group (0.24-fold expression; p = 0.002; Figure 9C).

entries.proposition: Supplement Table S1 gives the Wwox probe's per-animal normalised log-scale intensities (ONA 6.80, 7.36, 6.77; control 8.35, 7.56, 8.30), raw p 0.030, FDR-adjusted p 0.187 and Bonferroni p 1; the tabulated 0.864 equals the ratio of the two group means of these log-scale values (6.977 / 8.072), whose linear equivalent is about 0.47 (reader's arithmetic from these cells).
entries.anchor: Supplement Table S1, sheet 'analysis normalized', row 281 (columns: probe, ONA 15/19/17, CO 20/16/18, p-value, p_fdr, p_bonferroni, FC ONA vs CO)

entries.proposition: Whole-retina RT-qPCR used three to four retinae per group.
entries.snippet: Each RT-qPCR was performed in duplicates from each retina (n = 3–4/group).

entries.proposition: The authors' only interpretation of Wwox is a suggested regulatory role in the retina, drawn from prior literature, not from a test in this study.
entries.snippet: The findings of previous studies and our results have in common that loss of Wwox can affect and alter various components of the central nervous system, suggesting a regulatory role of Wwox in the retina.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on Gdf15 and Wwox

entries.proposition: Figure 9C: the immunised-group Wwox box lies wholly below the control line at 1, median about 0.22, box from about 0 to about 0.74, whisker to about 0.85; marked **.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation — pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 9C (Wwox): one ONA box plot; median line at about 0.22, box from about 0 to about 0.74, upper whisker about 0.85; dotted control line at 1; marked **.
